title: Determinism, Nondeterminism and Agent Action
results: Same Operation identity does not imply same result or same physical realization.
Determinism is relative to a modeled state/input/semantic boundary.
Repeatability, reproducibility, request replay, re-execution and result reproduction are distinct.
Reproducibility requires declared source/environment/instruction semantics and an output equivalence relation.
Hermeticity is dependency closure from undeclared ambient influence and is distinct from deterministic computation.
Dependency closure and sandboxing improve reproducibility without automatically eliminating timestamps, randomness or other nondeterminism.
Current exact replay returns the original durable Job/history and deliberately does not re-execute.
A new physical re-execution is a new historical action that may observe a changed world.
Current Operation identity binds important explicit proposal/source/environment/executable/provider/input semantics but is not a complete world-state key.
sourceStateDigest intentionally excludes ignored caches/build outputs, so source identity is not complete execution-state identity.
Ignored state can remain causally relevant if target code reads it.
Executable/provider commitments close selected realization machinery but not transitive toolchain, kernel, CPU or arbitrary external-service state.
Host Dependencies and immutable inputs provide stronger closure for named dependency classes without universal environment closure.
Environment construction/fixing reduces ambient variation but process environment is only one execution-state dimension.
Wall clock remains open target-observable input; Runtime timestamps and monotonic deadlines are evidence/control rather than time virtualization.
Kernel RNG is a deliberate nondeterministic input and can vary between otherwise equivalent realizations.
A fixed seed controls one randomness dimension but not scheduling, platform variation or independent randomness sources.
Internal concurrency/scheduling can make identical explicit inputs realize different histories/results.
execPlan fixes ordered control structure while constituent process behavior and data values remain potentially nondeterministic.
Filesystem metadata/order/pathnames and persistent/shared caches can be material execution-state inputs depending on workload.
Network and arbitrary external-service responses remain open-world inputs absent version/snapshot/recording contracts.
Recording external responses can convert one live dependency into frozen historical input but universal deterministic replay is costly and effect-sensitive.
Agent/model policy introduces higher-layer nondeterminism; Runtime freezes the submitted mechanical proposal rather than the reasoning policy that chose it.
Runtime should often preserve actual nondeterministic realization evidence rather than attempt universal elimination of variation.
Determinism and reproducibility are orthogonal to correctness, semantic success and auditability.
Nondeterminism can be intentional and useful; only material variation relative to the consumer contract needs control.
Freezing more state has compatibility, freshness, storage and complexity costs.
A consumer-specific determinism budget identifies which state dimensions must be fixed, recorded or virtualized.
Host currently owns reproduction/falsification experiments across multiple Runtime Operations while Runtime supplies exact mechanical evidence.
The governing law is DeterminismClaimScope <= ControlledStateBoundaryScope.

nextRound.title: External World and Open-System Effects
nextRound.entryQuestion: When Runtime crosses into independently changing external domains, what can it control, identify, observe, prove and reconcile without collapsing request, provider acceptance, external transition and semantic outcome?

notes: RF14 explains determinism/reproducibility/replay boundaries but does not authorize deterministic replay, clock/RNG virtualization, hermetic execution, cache redesign, model-sampling controls or production API changes.
